title: Infra: GPU Fleet Capacity, Cloud Accounts & IaC Strategy (Team Wiki & Runbooks)
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates our current infrastructure engineering guidance for GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform / IaC modules, CI/CD and build pipelines, and operational runbooks. It is intended as the single source of truth for the infra team and adjacent owners (SRE, serving-runtime, and platform).

Scope and intent:
- Audience: Infra engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and on-call responders.
- Scope: GPU fleet sizing and autoscaling, account topology and cross-account patterns, Terraform module conventions, CI/CD for infra changes, and runbooks for routine and incident operations.
- Out of scope: Application-level autoscaling policies (handled by serving teams) and vendor-specific procurement process.

Ownership:
- Primary owners: Infra Engineering (owner_team: engineering).
- Day-to-day steward: GPU Fleet WG (rotating lead).
- On-call: infra-oncall (pager rotation; see team wiki for schedule).

Key SLOs & Thresholds (production):
- GPU allocation success rate: 99.9% monthly (measured by scheduling API returning assigned GPU within 30s).
- Job queue p95 scheduling latency: <= 30s under normal load.
- Fleet-wide GPU utilization target: 60%–80% (keep headroom for bursts and pre-emption recovery).
- Scale-up trigger: queue depth > 50 pending pods for 5m AND average GPU utilization > 75% for 5m.
- Scale-down trigger: average GPU utilization < 50% for 10m AND queue depth < 5.

Fleet sizing methodology (how we decide capacity):
1. Baseline demand: aggregate historical peak 7-day rolling GPU-hours by region and workload class.
2. Safety headroom: baseline * 1.25 for burst tolerance and model hot-reloads.
3. Redundancy: reserve at least N+1 availability zone redundancy for Dedicated fleets and prefer AZ spread for Hosted.
4. Preemption tolerance: when using spot/preemptible capacity, add 15% additional on-demand reserved buffer for critical SLAs.

Instance mix guidance (example):
- Heavy inference (Larger models, KV cache-friendly): NVIDIA A100 / H100 class (p4/p5) with 80GB or 80–96GB variants.
- Cost-sensitive embeddings/batching: NVIDIA A10/A30 class.
- Development / CI: smaller GPU shares (T4/A2) in non-prod.
Decision: use a mix of reserved capacity for baseline (20–50% depending on contract) + spot/preemptible for burst.

Cloud accounts & networking patterns:
- Account topology: one infra (shared tooling) account per cloud + environment-specific accounts (prod, staging, dev) per region.
- VPC design: dedicated VPC per environment with standardized subnet CIDR allocations and explicit AZ mapping.
- Private connectivity: Transit gateway / Shared VPC for cross-account service-to-service traffic; use VPC endpoints for cloud APIs where supported.
- Security groups / NSGs: minimal exposure; GPU fleet nodes accept traffic only from LB and internal subnets.
- Peering & egress control: egress through NAT gateways with logging; critical paths also use private service endpoints.
- IAM patterns: least privilege roles, role-per-service model, cross-account assume-role for deployment pipelines. Use short-lived credentials via OIDC where possible.

Networking example (high-level):
- Prod VPC: 10.10.0.0/16
  - Public subnets: 10.10.0.0/24, 10.10.1.0/24 (bastion, jump proxies)
  - Private compute subnets (AZ-a): 10.10.10.0/24
  - Private compute subnets (AZ-b): 10.10.11.0/24
  - Storage & control plane: 10.10.20.0/24

Terraform / IaC conventions and modules:
Principles:
- Small focused modules (1 responsibility per module).
- Modules must be documented with inputs/outputs and example usage.
- All environment-specific configuration should be provided by a top-level stage repo (prod/staging/dev) - do not hardcode in modules.
- Use TF Registry style versioning + anchored tags (vX.Y.Z).

Primary module inventory (examples):
- infra-networking (vpc, subnets, route tables, endpoints)
- infra-gpu-cluster (ASG / node pools, node templates, autoscaling policies)
- infra-kms (KMS keys and grants for clusters and secrets)
- infra-iam (roles, instance profiles, OIDC providers)
- infra-monitoring (metrics exporters, pushgateway config, dashboards)
- infra-ci-cd (pipeline resources, cross-account deployment roles)

Example module usage (AWS, abbreviated):
```hcl
module "gpu_cluster" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.company.com/infra/modules/infra-gpu-cluster.git?ref=v1.3.0"
  name   = "gpu-cluster-prod-eu-west-1"
  instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge", "p4de.24xlarge"]
  desired_capacity = 50
  min_size = 10
  max_size = 200
  use_spot = true
  spot_percentage = 60
  subnets = module.vpc.private_subnets
  tags = var.common_tags
}
```

Module review checklist (PR requirements):
- Module includes README, examples, inputs/outputs documented.
- Tests: terratest or unit plan smoke tests in the pipeline.
- Security review: check KMS usage and IAM policies for least privilege.

CI/CD and build pipelines (infra changes):
Best practices:
- All infra changes flow through repo-based PRs with pipeline-enforced checks.
- Environments: plan-only runs on PRs; apply runs require merge to environment branch + approval from approvers list.
- Gate: terraform fmt, terraform init -upgrade -backend-config, plan and policy checks (Sentinel/OPA), and terratest integration for critical modules.
- Automatic drift detection: nightly terraform plan and alerting for drift > threshold (e.g., 5 resources).

Example pipeline steps (GitHub Actions / runner):
1. Checkout 
2. Run tflint and terraform fmt check
3. terraform init + terraform validate
4. terraform plan (store plan artifact)
5. Run policy checks (OPA Conftest / Sentinel emulation)
6. Post plan as PR comment and required approvals
7. On merge to env branch: terraform apply (requires 2 approvers for prod)

Testing infra changes (quick guide):
- Local: terraform plan + local terratest (if heavy, run on CI with a test account).
- Integration: run against staging environment with reduced capacity and no public-facing resources.
- Canary apply: for infra-gpu-cluster changes, roll 10% of nodes via instance template change and monitor metrics for 30m before full apply.

Runbooks (operational procedures):
1) Routine scale-up (capacity request / emergency):
- Trigger: exec-level finance-approved request OR automated alert (queue depth triggers).
- Steps:
  1. Open ticket in #infra-ops with expected window, rationale, target region, requested capacity (GPU count and instance types).
  2. Verify current utilization: grafana -> gpu-fleet -> region -> check p95 queue time and utilization.
  3. Create a change PR in infra/stage repo to increase desired_capacity or max_size in the infra-gpu-cluster module.
  4. Run plan in dev/staging to validate.
  5. Apply to prod during maintenance window (or emergency window if urgent). Monitor for errors and rollback plan prepared.
  6. Update tracking doc and notify stakeholders.

2) Incident: GPU allocation failures (runbook):
- Symptoms: scheduler returns allocation errors, significant backlog, p95 scheduling latency > 2m.
- Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
  - Pager to oncall -> acknowledge in PagerDuty.
  - Run: kubectl get pods -n gpu-system -o wide | grep Pending to identify failing reason.
  - Check autoscaler logs: kubectl logs deployment/gpu-autoscaler -n infra-controllers 
  - Check cloud provider limits: describe account quotas (AWS: ec2-service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-xxxxx)
  - If quota exhausted, open cloud support request and: increase desired_capacity to fallback smaller instance types if safe.
- Mitigations: temporarily set spot_percentage=0 for target ASG, increase on-demand reserved pool, or enable pre-warmed standby pool (N+1 nodes).
- Post-incident: run RCA template, update capacity runway calculations, and adjust thresholds if needed.

3) Node replacement & kernel/driver upgrades:
- Plan: rolling replacement with maxUnavailable = 10% and cordon+drain for each node.
- Steps:
  1. Create PR with new AMI/instance-template in infra-gpu-cluster module.
  2. Apply to a canary subset (10% nodes).
  3. Monitor metrics for 60m (GPU health, kernel oops, driver errors).
  4. Proceed in 3 phases: canary -> batch 50% -> remaining.

Operational dashboards and alerts (recommended):
- Dashboards: gpu-fleet-overview, queue-latency-by-workload, instance-health-by-az, spot-eviction-trends.
- Alerts:
  - Allocation-failure-rate > 0.1% sustained for 5m -> P1
  - queue-p95 > 60s for 10m -> P1
  - AZ capacity imbalance (>30% of fleet in single AZ) -> P2
  - Unexpected spot eviction spike (>10% in 5m) -> P2

Cost controls & observability:
- Tagging: required tags on all resources (team, cost-center, env, project, owner). Failure to tag blocks apply in CI via pre-commit checks.
- Cost dashboard: daily cost rollups by cluster and instance type.
- Optimization cadence: monthly review of spot/ondemand mix and model placement (move low-latency tolerant workloads to cheaper instance classes).

Access & security considerations:
- KMS keys: per-environment keys with key rotation policy 365 days.
- Secrets: use Secrets Manager / Vault; do not store credentials in TF state. Remote state backend must be encrypted and access-controlled.
- Remote state: S3 (encrypted) + DynamoDB lock for AWS; GCS + IAM locking for GCP.
- Audit: enable CloudTrail / Audit Logs for all infra accounts and forward to central logging with 365-day retention for prod.

Onboarding checklist for new infra engineers:
- Access: request access to infra repo, terraform state access, and cloud accounts via internal access flow.
- Runbooks: read this page + gpu runbook + CI/CD pipeline guide.
- Local tooling: install tfenv, terraform (locked version), terragrunt if used, awscli/gcloud, and kubectl configured for infra accounts.
- First run: deploy a small non-prod GPU pool in a sandbox account using infra-gpu-cluster module example and observe metrics.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Check pending pods:
  kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n gpu-workloads -o wide
- Increase cluster desired capacity (example terraform update workflow):
  git checkout -b infra/gpu-increase-202602
  edit modules/infra-gpu-cluster/variables.tf (desired_capacity)
  terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars
- Check spot eviction metrics (example cloud CLI):
  aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name SpotInstanceRequestsFulfilled --start-time ...

References and related pages:
- infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026 (module reference and deep dive)
- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 (operational runbook canonical)
- infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-and-iac-strategy-2026 (capacity strategy brief)

Change log:
- 2025-11-15: Initial draft (Priya Kapoor).
- 2026-01-12: Added CI/CD gating recommendations and canary apply steps (Ethan Zhang review).
- 2026-02-10: Finalized SLO numbers and incident runbook clarifications (Marisol Rivera review).

If anything in this document is unclear or requires more detail, add a comment or open a PR against the team wiki.
